source_uses.fact: Planning should consider noise created by development and sensitivity to the prevailing and anticipated acoustic environment
2022 round-4 strategic noise maps provide a snapshot of estimated road and rail noise across England using 2021 exposure conditions
Strategic mapping is GIS/modelled evidence and is not a parcel-specific acoustic survey
Road-noise collection was last updated 24 March 2026 and contains strategic indicators from 2022 analysis
Rail-noise collection was last updated 24 March 2026 and contains strategic indicators from 2022 analysis
Noise Action Planning Important Areas dataset identifies priority areas and was updated 11 September 2025
Adopted London Plan Policy D13 applies the Agent of Change principle to new noise-sensitive development
Adopted Policy D14 requires development to avoid significant adverse noise effects and use design-led mitigation
Housing Design guidance recommends early acoustic consideration and notes strategic Defra maps exclude some sources such as industrial and aircraft noise
Environmental Noise Regulations require regular noise mapping and action planning for transport noise
The 2026 London Plan is still at draft consultation stage and cannot replace adopted D13/D14 until formally adopted
Statutory consultation on the 2026 Draft London Plan runs from 16 July 2026 and the draft remains non-adopted

examples: Strategic road-noise mapping is a modelled area snapshot and not a façade or boundary measurement
Strategic rail-noise mapping does not include every local source or future operational change
An Important Area is a policy/action-planning signal and not proof that a candidate parcel fails acoustically
Agent of Change assigns mitigation responsibility but does not quantify a parcel mitigation cost
Policy D14 requires scheme-specific design evidence rather than a binary map-only score
Housing Design guidance says acoustics should be considered early for sites close to major noise sources
A quiet-looking strategic map cell cannot prove absence of industrial, construction or local plant noise
No promotion without a parcel/site relation plus scheme-specific acoustic assessment where relevant
